paths.description: Public landing page and primary upload entry point; represents marketing and first-use task discovery.
Plan comparison and commercial decision journey.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored.
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the body remained rgb(255,255,255), color-scheme computed to normal, and the dark screenshot was visually identical to light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not stop non-essential pulsing.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, getAnimations() still reported the 4,000 ms buttonPulse animation running.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animation inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: Route changes use abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.evidence: CSS/platform inspection found no view-transition rules while primary navigation uses ordinary cross-document links.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The very long landing page offers no position-aware navigation.
findings.evidence: The mobile landing page is 11,442 px tall, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state, progress, or sticky position feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight scroll-state-aware chrome or section progress cues for the long page.

findings.summary: Overlays are hand-built divs rather than platform primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found two div role=dialog elements with manual onclick dismissal and iframe content; no dialog or popover primitives were used.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover for transient UI, with declarative light dismiss and focus handling.

findings.summary: The cookie banner obscures primary content on every tested entry state.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a fixed consent banner covering the lower 90-190 px, including pricing CTA content and login secondary actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent control with equivalent accept/reject choices.

findings.summary: Two representative templates overflow the mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, pricing and about layout captures reported scrollWidth 370 vs clientWidth 360, a 10 px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the 370 px minimum/fixed width and use intrinsic fluid sizing.

findings.summary: Reusable components depend only on viewport-era CSS.
findings.evidence: Loaded CSS inspection found zero @container rules and zero logical sizing patterns despite cards and controls being reused across templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt size container queries for reusable cards and navigation components.

findings.summary: Several visible links have undersized touch boxes.
findings.evidence: Geometry probe found footer and policy links only 15-21 px tall, below a comfortable touch target, though keyboard focus on the main CTA was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas to at least 24x24 CSS px, ideally 44x44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The primary “Upload Files Now” action hides an account/captcha detour.
findings.evidence: The CTA href says /upgrade/, its form action is /trial_account_signup.php, and activating it opens an invisible reCAPTCHA instead of a file picker or clearly explained signup step.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename the action to set expectations or begin with a transparent signup step, then expose upload immediately after completion.

findings.summary: The 404 state provides weak recovery.
findings.evidence: A real HTTP 404 displays only a JavaScript history Back link and instructions to contact the administrator; there is no home, search, or relevant destination CTA, and the title remains generic.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide direct home/help/search links and a page-specific title while preserving the 404 status.

findings.summary: Lab loading performance misses the LCP and responsiveness bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.2 s, TBT 350 ms, and time-to-interactive 12.4 s (performance 0.62); the independent trace measured FCP/LCP 2.82 s and one 120 ms task.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource and defer non-critical scripts and trackers.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is dominated by scripts and blocking legacy resources.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 79 requests and 1.60 MB transferred, including 1.34 MB of script; parser-blocking jQuery 1.7.2 and reCAPTCHA plus three blocking stylesheets were confirmed in the DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Load reCAPTCHA on intent, remove parser-blocking legacy jQuery, and defer or eliminate non-critical scripts/styles.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 707 KiB unused JavaScript and 90 KiB unused CSS; the HAR shows repeated analytics/tag-manager payloads among the largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific bundles and remove duplicate analytics and unused legacy CSS/JS.

findings.summary: Heading semantics include an empty visible H1 alongside the content H1.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found a visible logo H1 with no text plus the actual page H1; Lighthouse otherwise reported accessibility 1.00 and logical heading order.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a non-heading logo wrapper and retain one descriptive H1 per page.

findings.summary: Platform hygiene is dated and blocks browser optimisations.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three deprecated API warnings, three BFCache failure reasons, two large scripts without valid source maps, and an inspector issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated APIs/listeners that block BFCache and publish valid source maps for maintained first-party bundles.

findings.summary: Distinct public pages reuse the homepage title and description.
findings.evidence: The About page and real 404 both report “File sharing and storage made simple”; About also reuses the generic homepage meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every public template a unique descriptive title and matching description.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no canonical link and /sitemap.xml returns HTTP 404, while robots.txt permits the public site.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap and self-referencing canonical URLs for indexable templates.

findings.summary: Organization metadata is shareable but not structured.
findings.evidence: Open Graph metadata is present, but no JSON-LD or other schema.org data was found on the organization homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD matching visible content.

findings.summary: Transport hardening and cookie flags are materially weak.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but HSTS is max-age=0, CSP only declares frame-ancestors, nosniff/referrer/permissions policies are absent, and 9 cookies were flagged insecure including ukey without Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable effective HSTS, deploy a restrictive CSP and baseline security headers, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with appropriate SameSite.

findings.summary: Tracking starts before meaningful consent and dominates transfer cost.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 17 third-party origins and six known trackers; HAR attributed 61 requests and 1.56 MB to third parties while the consent banner was still visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential analytics behind explicit consent and consolidate/remove overlapping trackers.

findings.summary: Authentication is password/social-only and disables password-manager hints.
findings.evidence: The login page exposes email/password and social providers but no passkey/WebAuthn flow; password autocomplete is explicitly off.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys and use autocomplete=current-password/username while keeping social options.

findings.guidanceId: offline fallback service worker web app manifest installable pwa
findings.summary: The app-like storage service has no install/offline surface.
findings.evidence: No web app manifest was linked and no service worker controlled the page; the product promotes ongoing file access across devices.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a manifest and service worker with an honest offline shell/fallback for previously available content.

findings.summary: The translated surface is not bidirectionally robust.
findings.evidence: The site exposes a large language selector and lang=en-US, but loaded CSS used physical left/right properties and zero logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS logical properties and verify translated/RTL layouts rather than relying solely on machine translation.

findings.summary: Commercial data is hard-coded to US dollars.
findings.evidence: Pricing displays $5.83/month and $6.99 month-to-month while offering hundreds of languages, with no locale/currency alternative visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Format currency and recurring price terms from locale-aware structured data using Intl.NumberFormat.

findings.summary: Consent uses implied acceptance with no equivalent reject choice.
findings.evidence: The banner says continued use means agreement, offers “I Accept” and a dismiss X but no reject/manage option, while tracker evidence confirms analytics already fires.
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit opt-in for non-essential tracking with equally prominent accept and reject/manage choices.

findings.summary: Sign-in obstructs autofill.
findings.evidence: The email field has no autocomplete token and the password field sets autocomplete=off, despite being a standard sign-in form.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password; do not suppress password managers.

findings.summary: Background analytics work is disproportionate to the landing page.
findings.evidence: Six tracker families execute on load; third-party transfers total 1.56 MB and include overlapping Google tags, Hotjar, Amplitude, DoubleClick and Cloudflare analytics.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate telemetry, batch what remains, and load it only after consent/idle.
